interpreted_annotation.note: Interpretive: this layer says that an occurrence IS the function the pattern was cut from, and that a miss means the function moved rather than that it is gone. Both lean on the pattern's provenance and on the assumption that the compiler did not emit the same bytes elsewhere. The primitive half -- the bytes found at the offsets -- is in literal_reads[].

evidence.note: 12 bytes at offset 19665984 of MISERY-Win64-Shipping.exe are 4883ec38488d05e539bb044c. This record gives the position and the extent, and nothing else. Method re-run and reproduced within this run: every range in this group was read a second time through a second, independently opened file handle and the two reads agree byte for byte. The limit of that attestation, stated plainly: it is a re-read of the same file on the same machine, so it catches a transient read, a seek error and a bookkeeping mistake -- it does not catch reading the wrong file.

refutation_probes.note: 1048565 occurrences of a 12-byte all-wildcard pattern in a 1048576-byte window; 1048565 expected (one per position that can hold the pattern)
refutation_probes.question: does the matcher find a pattern that constrains nothing, at every position of a bounded window?

window.note: the first 1048576 bytes of the first surface range

refutation_probes.would_refute: an all-wildcard pattern matching once, or not at all, would mean the matcher is selective for reasons other than the pattern, and every verdict in this document would be void

refutation_probes.note: 0 of 5 flipped patterns still matched somewhere on the surface
refutation_probes.question: with a single literal byte inverted, does each pattern become absent?
refutation_probes.would_refute: a flipped pattern that still matches somewhere would mean the surviving literal bytes, not the pattern as written, are doing the work

refutation_probes.note: 0 of 5 four-byte prefixes came out with fewer than two occurrences
refutation_probes.question: is a four-byte prefix of each signature ambiguous, as a byte sequence that short must be on a large code surface?
refutation_probes.would_refute: a four-byte prefix coming out unique would mean the surface being searched is far smaller than surface.bytes_searched claims

refutation_probes.note: 0 of 5 counts changed when the buffer was reduced to 33 bytes
refutation_probes.question: does every verdict survive re-scanning with a buffer barely larger than the longest pattern?
refutation_probes.would_refute: any count that changes with the buffer size would mean the overlap or the de-duplication rule is wrong, and no verdict in this document could be trusted

refutation_probes.note: 5 of 5 signatures are unique on this surface
refutation_probes.question: how many signatures actually came out unique?
refutation_probes.would_refute: nothing on its own; this probe exists so the headline count cannot be quoted without its denominator

surface.definition: every section with raw data whose characteristics carry IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE or IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE
surface.not_searched: read-only and writable data, resources, the headers and any overlay -- a byte sequence present there is NOT counted by this run

verdict_definitions.absent: zero occurrences on the searched surface
verdict_definitions.ambiguous: two or more occurrences, or the occurrence counter reached its cap
verdict_definitions.unique: exactly one occurrence on the searched surface
